obligations.summary: Member States shall ensure their competent authorities establish at least one AI regulatory sandbox at national level that is operational by 2 August 2026.
exceptions: Obligation may be fulfilled by participating in an existing sandbox providing an equivalent level of national coverage.

obligations.summary: Member States shall ensure that competent authorities allocate sufficient resources to comply with Article 57 effectively and in a timely manner.
Member States shall ensure an appropriate level of cooperation between authorities supervising other regulatory sandboxes and the national competent authorities.

Competent authorities shall provide guidance, supervision and support within the AI regulatory sandbox with a view to identifying risks, in particular to fundamental rights, health and safety, testing, mitigation measures, and their effectiveness.

Competent authorities shall provide providers and prospective providers participating in the AI regulatory sandbox with guidance on regulatory expectations and how to fulfil requirements and obligations under this Regulation.

Upon request, the competent authority shall provide providers or prospective providers with written proof of activities successfully carried out in the sandbox and an exit report detailing activities, results and learning outcomes.

Market surveillance authorities and notified bodies shall take exit reports and written proof provided by national competent authorities positively into account with a view to accelerating conformity assessment procedures.

National competent authorities shall ensure that national data protection authorities and other relevant authorities are associated with the operation of the AI regulatory sandbox where the AI systems involve processing of personal data or fall under their supervisory remit.

National competent authorities shall have the power to temporarily or permanently suspend the testing process or sandbox participation if significant risks to health, safety, or fundamental rights cannot be effectively mitigated, and shall inform the AI Office of such decisions.

Providers and prospective providers participating in the AI regulatory sandbox shall remain liable under applicable Union and national liability law for any damage inflicted on third parties as a result of the experimentation.
exceptions: No administrative fines shall be imposed for infringements of this Regulation where prospective providers observe the specific plan, terms and conditions, and follow guidance given by the national competent authority in good faith.
No administrative fines shall be imposed regarding other Union and national law where other competent authorities were actively involved in supervision and provided guidance.

obligations.summary: National competent authorities shall coordinate their activities and cooperate within the framework of the Board.

National competent authorities shall inform the AI Office and the Board of the establishment of a sandbox, and the AI Office shall make publicly available and keep updated a list of planned and existing sandboxes.

National competent authorities shall submit annual reports to the AI Office and the Board from one year after sandbox establishment until termination, and a final report, covering progress, results, best practices, incidents, lessons learnt, and recommendations.
National competent authorities shall make annual reports or abstracts thereof publicly available online.

The Commission shall develop a single dedicated interface containing all relevant information related to AI regulatory sandboxes to allow stakeholder interaction and non-binding guidance on conformity of innovative AI-embedded products and services.
